tonight.headline: Week 1 is final
body: Every game is played. You took it by 62.5 — Jefferson 31.2 and Allen 35.7 did most of it, and Likely's 27.8 sat on your bench.
Nothing left to set this week. Everything below is about Week 2.

case.label: What won it
case.body: Allen 35.7 against a 19.6 projection and Jefferson 31.2 against 17.1. Two players beat their number by a combined 30.2, which is more than the margin.

case.label: What it cost
case.body: Isaiah Likely scored 27.8 on your bench while Kyle Pitts started and scored nothing. That is 27.8 points you owned and did not use, in a week you happened not to need them.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Nothing — this one is settled. The lesson carries to Week 2, where the same two tight ends are still on the roster.

doFirst.title: Claim Jalen Coker
doFirst.subtitle: Drop Stafford — he cannot start for you in any week this season.

case.label: The player
case.body: Eight catches, 138 yards, two touchdowns. He led every Panther in snaps (57) and routes run (40), ahead of Tetairoa McMillan's 56 and 39. That is a full-time route-runner, not a spike week.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Chem starts one quarterback and its flex takes RB and WR only, so there is no slot Stafford can ever fill. He is 92.8% rostered because most leagues can use him; yours is not one of them.

case.label: The bye
case.body: Josh Allen's Week 7 bye is coverable with a free claim when it arrives, because priority here resets every week. That reset is the whole reason this drop is safe.

case.label: The clock
case.body: 07:00 UTC is 01:00 Wednesday in your time. If you wait until Wednesday morning it has already happened.

case.label: The counter
case.body: Sports Illustrated read the same game and call McMillan the primary target. I take the other side on the route count — but you should know the read is contested.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: McMillan reasserts and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across Weeks 2 and 3, or the Week 1 line proves to have been garbage-time inflated.

doFirst.title: Start Likely over Pitts
doFirst.subtitle: Week 2 tight end. The projections split them by 0.3; the reporting does not.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Likely caught all eight balls thrown at him for 78 yards and two touchdowns, on 49% of snaps. Three years and $40M to follow Harbaugh, and the first full-time tight end role of his career.

case.label: The correction
case.body: Yesterday's version of this card read Pitts as having lost his role. He has not — he ran a route on 81% of Atlanta's dropbacks, seventh among all Week 1 tight ends. What killed him was the quarterback.

case.label: The quarterback
case.body: Tua was ruled out Thursday with an oblique, Penix is inactive and says he is not back to 100%, and Cooper Rush went 12 of 22 for 144. Atlanta's Week 2 starter is still unresolved.

case.label: Against the numbers
case.body: This overrides ESPN, which prefers Pitts 181.4 to 156.2 for the season and ranks him TE7 to Likely's TE12.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Tua returns and Pitts clears five targets in Week 2, or Nabers reaches full health and Likely's route share falls under about 60%.

doFirst.title: Stefon Diggs
doFirst.subtitle: Only if you are outbid for Coker. Not both.

case.label: Why he is here
case.body: You dropped him on Saturday. On Sunday he drew nine targets and scored in his Washington debut, while Terry McLaurin — your flex — drew four for two catches and 14 yards.

case.label: Why not both
case.body: Winning one claim drops you to last for this waiver period. Order Coker first; this card exists for the morning you lose him.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Coker's claim processes. Then this card is moot and should not be fired.

whatWentWrong.title: You dropped Diggs one day early
whatWentWrong.lead: Cut Saturday. Sunday he drew nine targets and scored.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Diggs went 4 of 6 for 55 and a touchdown in his Commanders debut. McLaurin, who starts in your flex, went 2 of 4 for 14.

case.label: Why it matters
case.body: Washington signed Diggs in August into a room that already had McLaurin, Deebo Samuel and Zach Ertz. Week 1 is the first evidence of what that costs the player you own.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: McLaurin clears eight targets in Week 2. One game against a Seattle secondary that locked him up is not a trend yet.

whatWentWrong.title: Both tight ends scored zero
whatWentWrong.lead: Neither lost his role. Hold both, and start the right one.

case.label: Pitts
case.body: 0 for 1, but a route on 81% of dropbacks, seventh among Week 1 tight ends. His one target was an underthrown deep ball that scores if it is placed.

case.label: The cause
case.body: Atlanta were down to their third-string quarterback. That is a quarterback problem wearing a tight end's box score.

case.label: What to do
case.body: Nothing on the wire. The answer is on your own bench and it is the card above.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Pitts's route share drops under 65% once Atlanta have a healthy quarterback.

whatWentWrong.title: You are three deep on Jacksonville
whatWentWrong.lead: D/ST, Thomas and Tuten all start for the same team.

case.label: The exposure
case.body: The Jaguars defence, Brian Thomas Jr. and Bhayshul Tuten are all Jacksonville. One bad game for that offence is three bad rows on your roster.

case.label: Week 7
case.body: That is the Jacksonville bye. Three of your players are out on the same Sunday. It is solvable in Week 7, not now — roles change and a plan made five weeks early usually solves a problem that no longer exists.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Thomas is claimed away as the Diggs drop, which reduces the exposure to two by itself.

roster.footnote: Every game is played, so every row shows its result and every row is dimmed. Nothing here is a decision any more.

case.label: The usage
case.body: He took the only goal-line snap in Week 1 and five of the team's eight short-yardage plays, while Tuten took 48% of snaps to his 41%.

case.label: Why it matters here
case.body: You own Tuten. Rodriguez is the player capping him, and owning both is the only way to own that backfield's touchdowns.

case.label: When to act
case.body: The day a roster spot opens, not before. Nothing on your bench is worth dropping for a handcuff.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 83.2% rostered nationally and sitting free in a ten-team league. That is normally the strongest signal a wire gives.

case.label: Why not
case.body: Chem's flex takes RB and WR only, so a third tight end has no route into your lineup at all. He would be a pure bench body.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only if the Likely call breaks. That card carries its own flip condition.

doNotChase.name: Michael Mayer
doNotChase.lead: The biggest riser on the wire and the one to leave alone.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 6.0 targets and 10.9 points per game without Bowers. 2.9 and 3.4 with him.

case.label: The news
case.body: Schefter reports a realistic chance Bowers returns in Week 2 at the Chargers. The market is pricing a box score the reporting has already moved past.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Bowers missing Week 2 as well, or Kubiak's two-tight-end usage keeping Mayer above five targets with Bowers active.

doNotChase.name: Kalif Raymond
doNotChase.lead: Nine targets in a 59-point blowout is not a role.

case.label: The context
case.body: One game with Odunze limited, and garbage-time volume in a game that was decided by the third quarter.

case.label: The honest version
case.body: Watch only — but free money if it repeats, which is why he is listed rather than hidden.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A second week over seven targets with Odunze healthy.

settled.title: Warren over Tuten in the RB2 slot
settled.result: Warren 10.3, Tuten 9.8. Out-touched him by five.

settled.title: Brian Thomas Jr. add off waivers
settled.result: 7.0 in a game Jacksonville led 24-0 at half.

settled.title: Drop Monangai for Tucker
settled.result: Monangai scored 20.4. Not acted on, no harm done.

cannotSee.label: Week 2 is reporting, not data
cannotSee.body: Week 2 kickoffs and opponents are not in the snapshot, so every Week 2 matchup above comes from reporting rather than from the file.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: The league only ever returns your own waiver claims. Being outbid is possible and unknowable, which is why the fallback card exists.

cannotSee.label: Trades are priced on one week
cannotSee.body: A single week of projections is the wrong unit for a trade, and the only one published.

cannotSee.label: Defence reads are judgement
cannotSee.body: It is Week 1. There is no sample yet, so every matchup grade is an opinion with a number attached.
